context_length: T5 relative position bias; longer sequences are embedded whole here
summary: The compact Ankh model: a small T5 protein LM whose recipe came out of more than twenty pretraining experiments, with 768-dim embeddings meant to stay competitive with much larger models.
architecture: T5 encoder-decoder with relative position bias, 48 encoder and 24 decoder layers. Only the encoder is used here (453M parameters), giving 768-dim per-residue embeddings.
pretraining_data: UniRef50, trained with JAX/Flax on Google TPU v4 pods.
pretraining_objective: T5-style denoising with 20% of residues masked as single-residue spans, reconstructed by the decoder with the paper's partial demasking.
key_innovations: Efficiency-first design: strong general-purpose performance with far fewer params/embedding dims than ProtT5/ESM
Systematic ablation of masking, depth, and width to optimize the recipe
when_to_use: When you want a cheap, low-dimensional (768) embedding that is still competitive; good for large-scale embedding or memory-constrained heads.
caveats: Smallest Ankh; may trail larger models on the hardest tasks. Single-sequence, sequence-only.

citations.title: Ankh: Optimized Protein Language Model Unlocks General-Purpose Modelling
